key_insight: Clinicians see automated facial-analysis pain assessment as a promising adjunct, especially for patients who cannot communicate well, but only if it is highly accurate and fits clinical workflow.
clinical_relevance: This survey suggests AI pain-monitoring tools may be most useful for nonverbal, cognitively impaired, or language-barrier patients, while requiring strong performance and fairness before routine adoption.
method: Cross-sectional survey at a tertiary academic medical center
Participants: physicians, advanced practice providers, and nurses
Assessed current pain-assessment practices and views on facial-analysis AI
evidence_signal: The study surveyed 87 eligible clinicians and found generally neutral-to-positive attitudes, with most respondents demanding at least 90% accuracy before routine use.
watch_item: Potential alert fatigue and unequal performance across patient groups could limit safe implementation if not addressed.
paper_title: Clinician Perspectives on Automated Facial Analysis for Pain Assessment: A Cross-Sectional Survey of Physicians, Advanced Practice Providers, and Nurses
